questions.q: How many bones is a newborn baby born with?
questions.fact: Many of a baby's bones fuse together as the child grows, leaving 206 in adults.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body called?
questions.fact: The stapes, or stirrup, is about 3 millimeters long and sits in the middle ear.

questions.q: What is the common name for the patella?
questions.fact: The kneecap protects the front of the knee joint.

questions.q: What is the common name for the clavicle?
questions.fact: The collarbone is one of the most commonly broken bones.

questions.q: What is the common name for the sternum?
questions.fact: The ribs connect to the breastbone at the front of the chest.

questions.q: What is the common name for the scapula?
questions.fact: The shoulder blade is a flat, triangle-shaped bone on your upper back.

questions.q: What is the common name for the coccyx?
questions.fact: The tailbone is made of a few small bones fused together.

questions.q: What is the only bone in the skull that can move?
questions.fact: The lower jaw is called the mandible.

questions.q: How many pairs of ribs do most people have?
questions.fact: A small number of people have an extra rib.

questions.q: What do we call the bones that make up the spine?
questions.fact: Most adults have 33 vertebrae, though some fuse together.

questions.q: What are the bones in your fingers and toes called?
questions.fact: Each finger has three phalanges, while each thumb has two.

questions.q: About how many bones are in one human hand, including the wrist?
questions.fact: Your two hands and wrists together have over a quarter of all your bones.

questions.q: What is the soft tissue inside many bones that makes blood cells called?
questions.fact: Bone marrow makes billions of new blood cells every day.

questions.q: What mineral makes bones hard and strong?
questions.fact: Milk, yogurt, cheese and leafy greens are good sources of calcium.

questions.q: What is the bendy tissue in your nose and ears called?
questions.fact: Cartilage also cushions the ends of bones in your joints.

questions.q: What connects bones to other bones at a joint?
questions.fact: Ligaments are tough bands that keep joints steady.

questions.q: What kind of joint is your shoulder?
questions.fact: Ball and socket joints let your arm swing in a full circle.

questions.q: What kind of joint is your knee?
questions.fact: Like a door hinge, your knee mostly bends in one direction.

questions.q: What kind of joint lets you shake your head no?
questions.fact: The pivot joint is between the top two bones of your neck.

questions.q: What is the name for a broken bone?
questions.fact: Broken bones heal by growing new bone tissue across the break.

questions.q: What is a sprain?
questions.fact: Ankles are the most commonly sprained joint.

questions.q: About how many muscles are in the human body?
questions.fact: Muscles make up roughly a third to two fifths of your body weight.

questions.q: What is the largest muscle in the human body?
questions.fact: The gluteus maximus is in your buttocks and helps you stand up and climb.

questions.q: What are the three types of muscle in the body?
questions.fact: Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart.

questions.q: Which type of muscle is found only in the heart?
questions.fact: Cardiac muscle never gets tired the way arm muscles do.

questions.q: What do we call muscles you can control on purpose, like in your arms?
questions.fact: Muscles in your stomach and blood vessels work without you thinking about them.

questions.q: What muscle is on the front of your upper arm?
questions.fact: The triceps on the back of the arm straightens your elbow.

questions.q: What large muscle group is on the front of your thigh?
questions.fact: Quadriceps means four heads, because it is made of four muscles.

questions.q: Which muscle under your lungs helps you breathe?
questions.fact: Hiccups are sudden spasms of the diaphragm.

questions.q: What are muscles in the body able to do?
questions.fact: Muscles work in pairs, one pulling one way and its partner pulling back.

questions.q: Which tendon at the back of your heel is the strongest in the body?
questions.fact: It is named after Achilles, a Greek hero whose heel was his only weak spot.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny tubes that connect arteries and veins?
questions.fact: Some capillaries are so thin that red blood cells pass through them one at a time.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood back to the heart?
questions.fact: Veins have valves that keep blood from flowing backward.

questions.q: What is the largest artery in the body?
questions.fact: The aorta carries blood out of the heart to the rest of the body.

questions.q: About how long would all your blood vessels stretch if laid end to end?
questions.fact: That is long enough to wrap around Earth more than twice.

questions.q: About how much blood does an adult have?
questions.fact: A child has less, depending on their size.

questions.q: About how many times does a resting adult heart beat each minute?
questions.fact: Children's hearts usually beat a bit faster than adults'.

questions.q: What is the liquid part of blood called?
questions.fact: Plasma is mostly water and makes up a little more than half of your blood.

questions.q: Which tiny blood cell pieces help blood clot when you get a cut?
questions.fact: Platelets stick together to plug the cut, then help form a scab.

questions.q: What color is human blood inside your body?
questions.fact: Veins look blue through the skin because of how light passes through skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

questions.q: What makes red blood cells red?
questions.fact: When hemoglobin picks up oxygen, it turns a brighter red.

questions.q: About how long does a red blood cell live?
questions.fact: Your body makes millions of new red blood cells every second.

questions.q: What are the four main blood types?
questions.fact: Each type can also be positive or negative.

questions.q: Which blood type is often called the universal donor?
questions.fact: In emergencies, O negative blood can be given to almost anyone.

questions.q: Who discovered the main human blood groups in 1901?
questions.fact: Knowing blood types made blood transfusions much safer.

questions.q: Which scientist showed in 1628 that the heart pumps blood around the body in a circle?
questions.fact: Before Harvey, many people thought the liver made new blood all the time.

questions.q: What do we call the pressure of blood pushing on artery walls?
questions.fact: Doctors measure blood pressure with an inflatable cuff around your arm.

questions.q: What can you feel at your wrist or neck that shows your heartbeat?
questions.fact: You can count your pulse for 15 seconds and multiply by 4 to find your heart rate.

questions.q: What tool do doctors use to listen to your heart and lungs?
questions.fact: The stethoscope was invented in France in 1816.

questions.q: What do heart valves do?
choices: Keep blood flowing in one direction
questions.fact: The lub-dub sound of a heartbeat is made by valves closing.

questions.q: Which side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
questions.fact: The left side pumps oxygen-rich blood out to the rest of the body.

questions.q: About how big is your heart?
choices: About the size of your head
About the size of a pea
About the size of a football
About the size of your fist
questions.fact: Your heart beats more than 100,000 times a day.

questions.q: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs called?
questions.fact: Lungs have hundreds of millions of alveoli, where oxygen passes into the blood.

questions.q: What is the tube that carries air from your throat to your lungs called?
questions.fact: The trachea is also called the windpipe and has rings of cartilage to keep it open.

questions.q: What gas do you breathe out that your body needs to get rid of?
questions.fact: Your cells make carbon dioxide when they turn food into energy.

questions.q: What is the voice box called?
questions.fact: Your vocal cords sit inside the larynx and vibrate to make sound.

questions.q: Which lung is a little smaller?
questions.fact: The left lung is smaller to make room for the heart.

questions.q: What is the flap that covers your windpipe when you swallow called?
questions.fact: When food goes down the wrong way, it is because the epiglottis did not close in time.

questions.q: What is the little dangly thing at the back of your throat called?
questions.fact: The uvula helps close off your nose when you swallow.

questions.q: What makes you yawn?
choices: Scientists are still not completely sure
questions.fact: Yawning is contagious, and even reading about it can make you yawn.

questions.q: What is a sneeze?
choices: A type of cough from the stomach
A sign of a broken bone
A reflex to clear your nose of irritants
questions.fact: A sneeze can blast air out at high speed, so cover it with your elbow.

questions.q: What is the largest internal organ in the body?
questions.fact: The liver can regrow when part of it is removed.

questions.q: Which organ makes bile to help digest fats?
questions.fact: Bile is stored in a small organ called the gallbladder.

questions.q: Which organ makes insulin to control blood sugar?
questions.fact: People with type 1 diabetes have a pancreas that does not make enough insulin.

questions.q: Which organ helps filter blood and fight infections and sits on the left side under the ribs?
questions.fact: People can live without a spleen, but they may get some infections more easily.

questions.q: Which small, finger-shaped pouch is attached to the large intestine?
questions.fact: When the appendix gets infected, it is called appendicitis and is often removed.

questions.q: Which organ stores urine until you go to the bathroom?
questions.fact: An adult bladder can hold about half a liter.

questions.q: What do we call the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder?
questions.fact: Each kidney has its own ureter.

questions.q: About how big is a kidney?
choices: About the size of a fist
About the size of a pea
About the size of a basketball
About the size of a car tire
questions.fact: Kidneys are shaped like beans, which is why some beans are called kidney beans.

questions.q: Can a person live with only one kidney?
questions.fact: Many people donate one kidney to someone who needs it.

questions.q: How long is the small intestine in an adult?
questions.fact: It is called small because it is narrow, not short.

questions.q: What are the tiny finger-like bumps lining the small intestine called?
questions.fact: Villi give the intestine a huge surface for soaking up food.

questions.q: What does the large intestine mainly do?
questions.fact: Trillions of helpful bacteria live in the large intestine.

questions.q: What liquid in your mouth starts breaking down food?
questions.fact: You make roughly a liter of saliva every day.

questions.q: What strong acid is in your stomach?
questions.fact: A thick layer of mucus keeps stomach acid from digesting your stomach itself.

questions.q: About how long does it take food to travel all the way through your digestive system?
questions.fact: Food usually spends a few hours in the stomach.

questions.q: What is the wave-like squeezing that moves food through your digestive system called?
questions.fact: Peristalsis works even if you are upside down.

questions.q: What are the proteins in your body that speed up digestion called?
questions.fact: Each enzyme does one special job, like breaking down starch or protein.

questions.q: What causes the rumbling sound in your stomach?
choices: Gas and liquid moving through your intestines
questions.fact: The scientific name for a tummy rumble is borborygmi.

questions.q: What is the largest part of the brain?
questions.fact: The cerebrum handles thinking, memory, speaking and movement.

questions.q: Which part of the brain helps control balance and coordination?
questions.fact: Cerebellum means little brain in Latin.

questions.q: Which part of the brain controls breathing and heartbeat?
questions.fact: The brain stem connects the brain to the spinal cord.

questions.q: Which side of the brain mainly controls the right side of the body?
questions.fact: The nerves cross over, so each half of the brain controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.q: About how much does an adult brain weigh?
questions.fact: The brain is about 2 percent of your body weight but uses about 20 percent of your energy.

questions.q: What are nerve cells called?
questions.fact: Your brain has about 86 billion neurons.

questions.q: How fast can signals travel along some nerves?
questions.fact: Fast nerve signals let you jerk your hand away from something hot almost instantly.

questions.q: What do we call a quick automatic movement, like jerking your hand away from something hot?
questions.fact: Some reflexes are handled by the spinal cord before the signal even reaches your brain.

questions.q: What happens when a doctor taps just below your kneecap?
choices: Your leg kicks out by reflex
questions.fact: This is called the knee-jerk reflex.

questions.q: What is the brain's fluid cushion called?
questions.fact: This clear fluid helps protect the brain from bumps.

questions.q: What are the folds and grooves on the brain's surface for?
choices: They pack more brain into the skull
questions.fact: If you could flatten out the brain's outer layer, it would be about the size of a pillowcase.

questions.q: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters by changing size?
questions.fact: Your pupils get bigger in the dark and smaller in bright light.

questions.q: What is the layer at the back of the eye that senses light?
questions.fact: The retina has millions of light-sensing cells called rods and cones.

questions.q: Which cells in your eyes help you see colors?
questions.fact: Most people have three types of cones, for red, green and blue light.

questions.q: Which cells in your eyes help you see in dim light?
questions.fact: Rods do not see color, which is why things look gray in very dim light.

questions.q: What is the clear front window of the eye called?
questions.fact: The cornea has no blood vessels and gets oxygen straight from the air.

questions.q: Which nerve carries signals from the eye to the brain?
questions.fact: Where the optic nerve leaves the eye, there is a blind spot with no light sensors.

questions.q: Does the image on your retina appear upside down?
choices: Yes, and your brain flips it
questions.fact: The lens of your eye bends light so the image lands upside down.

questions.q: What is it called when someone cannot tell certain colors apart, like red and green?
questions.fact: Color blindness is much more common in boys than in girls.

questions.q: What kind of glasses help people who cannot see faraway things clearly?
questions.fact: Being nearsighted means you see near things clearly but faraway things look blurry.

questions.q: Why do your eyes blink?
choices: To keep them moist and clean
questions.fact: Most people blink about 15 to 20 times a minute.

questions.q: What do tears do besides show feelings?
choices: Keep eyes wet and wash away dust
questions.fact: Tears also contain substances that fight germs.

questions.q: What are the three tiny bones in the middle ear?
questions.fact: Their scientific names are the malleus, incus and stapes.

questions.q: What is the snail-shaped part of the inner ear that helps you hear?
questions.fact: Tiny hair cells in the cochlea turn sound vibrations into nerve signals.

questions.q: What part of your body helps you keep your balance besides your eyes?
questions.fact: Fluid moving in your inner ear tells your brain how your head is moving.

questions.q: Why do you feel dizzy after spinning around?
choices: Fluid in your inner ear keeps moving after you stop
questions.fact: Your brain gets mixed signals from your eyes and inner ear.

questions.q: What thin layer of skin in the ear vibrates when sound hits it?
questions.fact: The eardrum passes vibrations on to the tiny bones of the middle ear.

questions.q: Why do your ears pop on an airplane?
choices: Air pressure inside and outside your ear evens out
questions.fact: Swallowing or yawning helps your ears pop.

questions.q: What is earwax for?
choices: Protecting and cleaning the ear canal
questions.fact: Doctors say you should not push cotton swabs deep into your ears.

questions.q: About how many taste buds does a person have?
questions.fact: Taste buds are replaced about every one to two weeks.

questions.q: What are the five basic tastes?
choices: Hot, cold, wet, dry and soft
Sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami
Sweet, spicy, crunchy, salty and sour
Red, green, blue, yellow and white
questions.fact: Umami is a savory taste found in foods like cheese, mushrooms and broth.

questions.q: Why does food taste bland when you have a cold?
choices: Much of flavor comes from your sense of smell
questions.fact: Holding your nose while eating shows how much smell matters for flavor.

questions.q: Is spicy heat from chili peppers a taste?
choices: No, it is a feeling of pain or heat
Yes, it is the sixth taste
Yes, it is a sweet taste
Only on the back of the tongue
questions.fact: A chemical in chili peppers called capsaicin tricks heat sensors in your mouth.

questions.q: Is the idea of a tongue map, with each taste in one area, correct?
choices: Yes, sweet is only at the tip
Yes, bitter is only on the sides
No, all areas of the tongue can sense all tastes
questions.fact: The tongue map myth came from a mistranslation of a German paper from 1901.

questions.q: About how many different smells can a human nose tell apart?
questions.fact: Some scientists think people may be able to detect over a trillion different smells.

questions.q: What is the name of the sense that tells you where your body parts are without looking?
questions.fact: It is why you can touch your nose with your eyes closed.

questions.q: What sense organ is your skin?
choices: It is not a sense organ
questions.fact: Your fingertips have some of the most touch sensors in your body.

questions.q: What is the outer layer of your skin called?
questions.fact: You shed tens of thousands of dead skin cells every minute.

questions.q: What gives skin its color?
questions.fact: Melanin also helps protect skin from the Sun's ultraviolet rays.

questions.q: What are freckles?
questions.fact: Freckles often get darker in summer after time in the sun.

questions.q: Why do you get goosebumps?
choices: Tiny muscles pull your hairs upright
questions.fact: In furry animals, raising the hair helps them stay warm or look bigger.

questions.q: Why do you sweat?
questions.fact: As sweat evaporates, it carries heat away from your skin.

questions.q: About how many sweat glands does a person have?
questions.fact: The palms of your hands and soles of your feet have the most.

questions.q: Why do your fingers get wrinkly in the bath?
choices: They soak up so much water they burst
Your nervous system makes them wrinkle
questions.fact: Scientists think wrinkly fingers may help grip wet things better.

questions.q: What are fingernails and hair made of?
questions.fact: Animal claws, hooves and horns are made of keratin too.

questions.q: Which grow faster, fingernails or toenails?
choices: They grow at the same speed
questions.fact: Fingernails grow about 3 millimeters a month.

questions.q: About how many hairs are on a person's head?
questions.fact: People with blond hair usually have more hairs on their heads than people with red hair.

questions.q: About how many hairs does a person normally lose each day?
questions.fact: New hairs grow back to replace the ones that fall out.

questions.q: Which part of the hair is alive?
questions.fact: The hair you can see is made of dead cells, so cutting it does not hurt.

questions.q: What makes fingerprints special?
choices: No two people have the same ones
questions.fact: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.

questions.q: At what age do most people's fingerprints form?
questions.fact: Fingerprints form in the womb, months before birth.

questions.q: What causes a bruise?
choices: Blood leaking from tiny broken vessels under the skin
questions.fact: Bruises change colors from purple to green to yellow as they heal.

questions.q: What is a scab?
choices: A dried blood clot that protects a cut while it heals
questions.fact: Picking scabs can slow healing and may leave a scar.

questions.q: What is the soft inside of a tooth with nerves and blood vessels called?
questions.fact: A toothache often happens when decay reaches the pulp.

questions.q: How many teeth does an adult usually have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.fact: Many people have their wisdom teeth removed because there is not enough room.

questions.q: What are the pointy teeth next to the front teeth called?
questions.fact: Canines are named after dogs, which have big pointy canine teeth.

questions.q: What are the flat front teeth used for biting called?
questions.fact: You have eight incisors, four on top and four on bottom.

questions.q: What are the big flat teeth at the back used for grinding food called?
questions.fact: Molar comes from the Latin word for millstone, a stone used to grind grain.

questions.q: What sticky film of germs on teeth causes cavities?
questions.fact: Bacteria in plaque eat sugar and make acid that wears away enamel.

questions.q: What should you use to clean between your teeth?
questions.fact: Floss reaches places a toothbrush cannot.

questions.q: At about what age do most kids start losing baby teeth?
questions.fact: The front teeth are usually the first to fall out.

questions.q: What is the body's system of glands that make hormones called?
questions.fact: Hormones are chemical messengers that travel in the blood.

questions.q: Which gland in the brain is sometimes called the master gland?
questions.fact: The pituitary gland is only about the size of a pea.

questions.q: Which hormone gives you a burst of energy when you are scared?
questions.fact: Adrenaline makes your heart pound and gets your body ready to fight or run.

questions.q: Which hormone helps make you sleepy when it gets dark?
questions.fact: Bright screens at night can lower melatonin and make it harder to fall asleep.

questions.q: Which gland in the neck controls how fast your body uses energy?
questions.fact: The thyroid is shaped a bit like a butterfly.

questions.q: What hormone tells your body to grow taller as a kid?
questions.fact: Much of your growth hormone is released while you sleep.

questions.q: What is the body's defense system against germs called?
questions.fact: Your immune system remembers germs it has fought before.

questions.q: What proteins does your immune system make to attack specific germs?
questions.fact: Vaccines teach your body to make antibodies without getting sick first.

questions.q: Why do you get a fever when you are sick?
choices: Your body heats up to help fight germs
questions.fact: A normal body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What is the normal human body temperature, about?
questions.fact: That is about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit, though normal can vary a little from person to person.

questions.q: What do vaccines do?
choices: Kill all bacteria in your body
Train your immune system to recognize a germ
questions.fact: Vaccines have prevented millions of deaths from diseases like measles and polio.

questions.q: What are the small bean-shaped lumps that filter germs and can swell when you are sick?
questions.fact: Swollen lymph nodes in your neck often mean your body is fighting an infection.

questions.q: What are the two lumps at the back of your throat that help fight germs?
questions.fact: Tonsils sometimes get infected and swollen, which is called tonsillitis.

questions.q: What is an allergy?
choices: When the immune system overreacts to something harmless
questions.fact: Pollen, peanuts and pet dander are common things people are allergic to.

questions.q: What is the common cold caused by?
questions.fact: Going outside with wet hair does not give you a cold, but germs from other people can.

questions.q: Why don't antibiotics cure colds?
choices: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only kill bacteria
questions.fact: Rest, fluids and time are the usual cure for colds.

questions.q: What is the best way to stop germs spreading when you cough?
choices: Hold your breath for a minute
Cough into your elbow or a tissue
questions.fact: Then wash your hands with soap and water.

questions.q: How long should you scrub your hands with soap?
questions.fact: That is about how long it takes to hum Happy Birthday twice.

questions.q: About how many cells are in the human body?
questions.fact: Red blood cells make up most of them by number.

questions.q: Which are the biggest cells in the human body?
questions.fact: A human egg cell is just barely big enough to see without a microscope.

questions.q: What is the longest cell in the human body?
choices: A nerve cell running down the leg
questions.fact: Some nerve cells stretch from the bottom of the spine to the toes, about a meter long.

questions.q: What carries the instructions that make you look like your family?
questions.fact: You get half of your DNA from each parent.

questions.q: How many chromosomes do most humans have in each cell?
questions.fact: Chromosomes come in 23 pairs.

questions.q: What is the name for twins that come from one egg and share almost the same DNA?
questions.fact: Fraternal twins come from two different eggs and are no more alike than other siblings.

questions.q: What do we call a feature, like eye color, that is passed from parents to children?
questions.fact: Freckles, dimples and earlobe shape can all be inherited traits.

questions.q: What are the six main types of nutrients your body needs?
choices: Sugar, salt, candy, chips, soda and water
Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water
questions.fact: A balanced diet gives your body all six.

questions.q: What is the main job of carbohydrates in food?
questions.fact: Bread, rice, pasta and fruit are full of carbohydrates.

questions.q: What is the main job of protein in your diet?
questions.fact: Beans, eggs, fish, meat and nuts are good sources of protein.

questions.q: Which vitamin helps your eyes see in dim light?
questions.fact: Carrots, sweet potatoes and spinach contain the building blocks for vitamin A.

questions.q: Which vitamin helps your blood clot?
questions.fact: Leafy green vegetables like kale and spinach are full of vitamin K.

questions.q: Which disease did sailors get long ago from not eating enough vitamin C?
questions.fact: British sailors were given limes to prevent it, which is why they were nicknamed limeys.

questions.q: Which disease, causing soft and bent bones, comes from not getting enough vitamin D?
questions.fact: Sunlight and foods like fish and fortified milk help prevent rickets.

questions.q: Which mineral helps your blood carry oxygen?
questions.fact: Not getting enough iron can make people feel tired, a condition called anemia.

questions.q: What fiber-rich foods help keep your digestion moving smoothly?
questions.fact: Fiber is a part of plants that your body cannot fully digest.

questions.q: About what fraction of the human body is water?
questions.fact: Babies have an even higher percentage of water than adults.

questions.q: About how long can a person survive without water?
questions.fact: In hot weather, the body loses water even faster.

questions.q: What is it called when your body does not have enough water?
questions.fact: Dark yellow urine and headaches can be signs you need to drink more water.

questions.q: What is a calorie?
choices: A unit of the energy in food
questions.fact: Kids who are active need more food energy than kids who sit a lot.

questions.q: What happens to extra food energy your body does not use right away?
choices: Much of it is stored as fat
questions.fact: Fat stores energy and also keeps your body warm.

questions.q: About how many hours of sleep do kids aged 6 to 12 need each night?
questions.fact: Sleep helps your brain store memories and your body grow.

questions.q: What is the stage of sleep when you dream the most called?
questions.fact: REM stands for rapid eye movement, because your eyes dart around under your eyelids.

questions.q: What happens to your muscles during REM sleep?
choices: Most of them become very relaxed and still
questions.fact: This stops you from acting out your dreams.

questions.q: What happens to your brain while you sleep?
questions.fact: Getting good sleep before a test can help you remember what you studied.

questions.q: Why does your stomach growl when you are hungry?
choices: Your stomach and intestines squeeze even when empty
questions.fact: The sounds are louder when your stomach is empty because there is nothing to muffle them.

questions.q: What is the medical name for the hiccups?
questions.fact: Hiccups happen when your diaphragm suddenly tightens and your vocal cords snap shut.

questions.q: What causes brain freeze when you eat something cold too fast?
choices: Blood vessels in your mouth and head reacting to the cold
questions.fact: Pressing your tongue against the roof of your mouth can help it go away faster.

questions.q: What is the funny bone?
choices: A nerve at your elbow, not a bone
questions.fact: Bumping the ulnar nerve against bone gives that tingly zap.

questions.q: Why does your foot fall asleep?
choices: Pressure squeezes nerves and blood vessels
questions.fact: The pins and needles feeling goes away when the pressure is gone.

questions.q: What is the body's largest gland?
questions.fact: The liver does more than 500 jobs, like cleaning blood and storing energy.

questions.q: What is the strongest muscle in the body based on its weight?
questions.fact: Your jaw muscles can bite down with surprising force.

questions.q: What is the hardest working muscle in the body?
questions.fact: The heart beats about 2.5 billion times over an average lifetime.

questions.q: What are the two bones in your lower leg?
questions.fact: The tibia, or shin bone, is the larger of the two.

questions.q: What are the two bones in your forearm?
questions.fact: The radius is on the thumb side of your arm.

questions.q: What is the bone in your upper arm called?
questions.fact: Its name sounds like humorous, which is one reason people call the elbow nerve the funny bone.

questions.q: What bones form your hips?
questions.fact: The pelvis is shaped like a bowl and supports your upper body.

questions.q: What is the name of the bone that protects the brain from the front, at the forehead?
questions.fact: The skull is made of many bones joined together by wavy seams called sutures.

questions.q: What are the soft spots on a baby's head called?
questions.fact: The soft spots let the skull squeeze a little during birth and let the brain grow.

questions.q: What happens to astronauts' bones in space?
questions.fact: Exercise helps astronauts slow down bone loss.

questions.q: What do bones do besides holding you up?
choices: Protect organs, make blood cells and store minerals
questions.fact: Bones are living tissue that can grow and heal.

questions.q: What is the main job of the skeletal system?
questions.fact: Without a skeleton, your body would collapse like a jellyfish.
